title: How Beauteous Were the Marks Divine
description: How Beauteous Were the Marks Divine in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Arthur Cleveland Coxe wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 124, “Divine Beauty of Christ's Character”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How beau-teous were the marks di-vine, That in thy meek-ness used to shine, That lit thy lone-ly path-way, trod In won-drous love, O Son of God!

lines: How beauteous were the marks divine,
That in thy meekness used to shine,
That lit thy lonely pathway, trod
In wondrous love, O Son of God!
O, who like thee, — so calm, so bright,
So pure, so made to live in light?
O, who like thee did ever go
So patient through a world of woe?
O, who like thee so humbly bore
The scorn, the scoffs, of men before?
So meek, forgiving, godlike, high,
So glorious in humility?
The bending angels stooped to see
The lisping infant clasp thy knee,
And smile, as in a father's eye,
Upon thy mild divinity.
And death, which sets the prisoner free,
Was pang and scoff and scorn to thee;
Yet love through all thy torture glowed,
And mercy with thy life-blood flowed.
O, in thy light be mine to go,
Illuming all my way of woe;
And give me ever on the road
To trace thy footsteps, Son of God!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Arthur Cleveland Coxe died in 1896.
credits: Words by Arthur Cleveland Coxe (1818–1896), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
